---
title: "Optimization and repeated runs"
description: "Configure methods and optimizers, use exaggeration, and compare repeated starts."
---

`smallvis` makes it possible to change the objective and optimizer independently. This is useful for
experiments, but a setting that works well for t-SNE need not work well for another cost function.
Start by changing one choice at a time, keeping preprocessing and initialization fixed.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(smallvis)
```

## Configure a method

Use a string for a method's defaults, or a list whose first element names the method and whose other
elements override its options. For example, this configures the balance of repulsion and attraction
in the LargeVis cost function:

```{r largevis}
largevis_fit <- smallvis(
  iris,
  method = list("largevis", gamma = 1),
  Y_init = "spca",
  perplexity = 30,
  eta = 0.1,
  max_iter = 1000,
  epoch_callback = FALSE,
  n_threads = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)
dim(largevis_fit)
```

The package implements the LargeVis and UMAP cost functions with its own optimization machinery.
These runs are different from the original algorithms' sampled stochastic optimization procedures.
The [LargeVis](largevis.html) and [UMAP](umap.html) articles examine those differences; the
[method-specific options](../reference/smallvis.html#method-specific-options) reference lists the
available controls.

## Change the optimizer

The default is the delta-bar-delta scheme familiar from t-SNE. The `opt` argument also accepts
optimizers provided through [mize](https://github.com/jlmelville/mize), with options supplied in a
list. For UMAP, t-UMAP, and LargeVis, function-based line searches require `gr_eps = 0` so the
gradient matches the objective used by the search:

```{r lbfgs}
umap_fit <- smallvis(
  iris,
  scale = FALSE,
  method = list("umap", gr_eps = 0),
  opt = list("l-bfgs", c1 = 1e-4, c2 = 0.9),
  Y_init = "spca",
  max_iter = 300,
  epoch_callback = FALSE,
  n_threads = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)
dim(umap_fit)
```

The [alternative optimizers](../reference/smallvis.html#alternative-optimizers) reference gives the
supported settings. Longer experiments compare [L-BFGS](opt.html),
[conjugate gradient](cg.html), [spectral directions](specd.html), and
[gradient-based adaptive updates](sgd.html).

## Use exaggeration

Early exaggeration strengthens attractive interactions for an initial phase. In this t-SNE run,
input probabilities are multiplied by 4 for the first 100 iterations:

```{r exaggeration}
exaggerated_fit <- smallvis(
  iris,
  Y_init = "spca",
  perplexity = 30,
  eta = 100,
  exaggeration_factor = 4,
  stop_lying_iter = 100,
  epoch_callback = FALSE,
  n_threads = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

`late_exaggeration_factor` and `start_late_lying_iter` enable a later phase; the
[late exaggeration experiments](lexagg.html) explore its effect. Function-based line searches are
restricted to configurations whose objective and gradient agree; smallvis reports unsupported
combinations rather than silently treating them as ordinary optimization.

## Compare random starts

`smallvis_rep()` runs from random initial coordinates and returns the result with the lowest final
cost. It overrides `Y_init`; built-in methods share one prepared input graph across the starts.
With `ret_extra = TRUE`, `all_costs` contains the final cost from each run:

```{r repeats}
set.seed(42)
best <- smallvis_rep(
  nrep = 3,
  X = iris,
  perplexity = 30,
  ret_extra = TRUE,
  epoch_callback = FALSE,
  n_threads = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)
best$all_costs
sum(best$costs)
```

This comparison holds the objective and affinities fixed. Costs from different methods or input
graphs generally have different meanings and should not be used as a universal embedding score.
Use `keep_all = TRUE` to inspect every layout; see the
[repeated-run reference](../reference/smallvis_rep.html).

## Step down through perplexities

`smallvis_perpstep()` starts with larger perplexities, then optimizes at the requested target. The
`step_iter` budget is taken out of `max_iter`, rather than added to it:

```{r stepping}
stepped_fit <- smallvis_perpstep(
  X = iris,
  Y_init = "spca",
  perplexity = 30,
  step_iter = 50,
  max_iter = 300,
  epoch_callback = FALSE,
  n_threads = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)
dim(stepped_fit)
```

The [perplexity-stepping reference](../reference/smallvis_perpstep.html) describes the schedule and
which controls apply to the final phase.
